# `Q-5-5` — Example Embed Target Is Not a Static Asset

> An `.embed-example-iframe` `file=` points at a source
> document (e.g. a `.qmd`) that would need rendering. The embed
> target must be a pre-rendered static asset, such as a `.html`
> file.

## What this means

An `.embed-example-iframe` embeds its `file=` target in an
`<iframe>`, resolving the path like any other project link.
The target must already exist as a **static asset** — Quarto
copies it into the rendered site and the browser loads it
directly. A `.qmd` (or other source document) is *not* static:
it would need to be rendered first, and an iframe cannot render
it on demand.

Requiring a static target also rules out a footgun: an iframe
whose target re-embeds the page that contains it would recurse.

## Why this happens

The most common cause is pointing `file=` at the example's
**source** instead of its **rendered output**:

```markdown
::: {.embed-example-iframe file="examples/presentations/03-fragments/slides.qmd"}
```

## How to fix

Point `file=` at the rendered output of the example, not its
source:

```markdown
::: {.embed-example-iframe file="examples/presentations/03-fragments/slides.html"}
[View source](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/examples/presentations/03-fragments)
:::
```

Make sure the rendered asset actually exists in the project
(render the example and stage its output) so the copied site
can resolve the frame.
